cases.title: Duplicate-ticket detection: where to put the threshold
cases.context_md: A support tool wants to show *“possible duplicate of #4812”* when an agent opens a new ticket. An engineer prototypes with a cosine threshold of 0.80 because “0.8 sounds high”. On real data, nearly every ticket gets flagged.

pipeline.detail: Ticket subject + first message, open-weights model, normalized
ANN top-5 among open tickets from the last 30 days
Suggestion to the agent, who decides

numbers.label: Unrelated-pair cosine
numbers.note: a compressed score range is common (anisotropy)

numbers.label: Labelled pairs needed
numbers.note: to pick a threshold with confidence

decision.prompt_md: How do you set the duplicate rule?

options.md: Keep 0.80; it worked for a blog post's examples
options.outcome_md: Thresholds are model- and domain-specific. This model's scores sit high, so 0.80 flags everything and agents learn to ignore the feature.

options.md: Label ~300 pairs, plot precision/recall against the threshold, pick the threshold that hits the precision target, and show results as a *suggestion*
options.outcome_md: The threshold now means something (“90% of flags are true duplicates”). Keeping a human in the loop makes the remaining errors cheap. Re-calibrate whenever the model changes.
Same-template tickets (*“Refund request for order …”*) score very high and differ only in the order number. Auto-merging destroys real tickets.

options.md: Use the embedding for candidates, then confirm with a cross-encoder classifier
options.outcome_md: More accurate, with a higher per-ticket cost. A good next step once you have labels from option B.

cases.lessons_md: A cosine value has no universal meaning. **Calibrate on labelled pairs for each model**, and prefer suggestions over automatic actions when errors are costly.

cases.title: Upgrading the embedding model under a live index
cases.context_md: An internal RAG assistant serves 50M chunks embedded with an older model. A newer model scores much better on the team's eval set. Leadership asks: *“Can we switch on Monday?”*

pipeline.detail: Tag every vector with model_id + version
Re-embed 50M chunks into a NEW index (resumable batch job)
New and updated docs go to both indexes during the backfill
Mirror live queries to the new index and compare
Alias swap, keeping the old index for rollback

options.md: “Yes: switch the query embedder on Monday.”
options.outcome_md: Queries in the new space against documents in the old space return effectively random results. The assistant confidently answers from irrelevant passages.

options.md: “We'll re-embed in place over the week.”
options.outcome_md: For the whole week the index mixes two spaces, and quality degrades unpredictably, query by query.

options.md: “We'll build a new index in parallel, shadow-test it, and cut over when the metrics hold, with rollback ready.”
options.outcome_md: No mixed-space window, a measured improvement, and a one-command rollback. It costs a few hundred dollars and a few days.

cases.lessons_md: **An embedding model upgrade is a data migration, not a config change.** Version every vector.
